subject: Materials Science
title: Thermal Conductivity and Expansion
description: Learn Thermal Conductivity and Expansion in one minute.

hook.text: A metal spoon in hot soup burns your hand. A wooden spoon doesn't. That's thermal conductivity.

buildup.text: Thermal conductivity measures how fast heat flows through a material — copper is 400 W/m·K, wood is 0.1.

discovery.text: In metals, free electrons carry most of the heat — that's why good electrical conductors are good heat conductors.

twist.text: Thermal expansion makes bridges grow in summer — the Golden Gate Bridge is 15 cm longer on hot days.

climax.text: Mismatched expansion cracks ceramic coatings on metal — matching thermal expansion is an engineering must.

punchline.text: Heat makes materials grow — and engineers must plan for every millimeter.

quiz.question: Why are metals usually good thermal conductors?
options: They are shiny and reflect heat inward
Free electrons carry heat efficiently through the lattice
They are denser than other materials
